_comment: Seed queries for discover.ts --search, one array per market. Derived from six of the eight topic slugs in config/taxonomy.yaml (linkedin-networking, interview-performance, resume-not-working, no-local-experience, volume-no-results, no-callbacks). visa-time-pressure and visa-pr-blocker are deliberately NOT represented here -- no visa, PR or sponsorship queries. Giving migration advice is regulated activity in Australia; this system does not participate in those conversations, same rule as the X channel strategy. Those two topic slugs remain valid classification labels for whatever content a non-visa query happens to surface -- they're just never the thing being searched for. Edit this file directly to retune queries; no code changes needed.
_comment_AU: Rewritten 2026-08-26 after the first AU sweep showed the original first-person-experience phrasing ('no Australian experience', 'why can't I get a job Australia') matched expat-lifestyle vloggers just as readily as coaching content -- only 6 of 37 gated candidates were genuine career coaches. Rewritten in practitioner/advice language (what a coach would title their own content: 'resume tips', 'how to get a job'), which a lifestyle vlogger captioning their own life story is far less likely to use incidentally. --classify is still the primary relevance fix; this rewrite is a secondary lever to raise the relevant fraction of what --search surfaces in the first place.
